candidate.analysis: The program reads only /input/public_csv, validates the expected fishing-trip fields, summarizes fish caught per hour, compares livebait and camper groups, and estimates associations using ordinary least squares when sufficient complete data are available. It prints concise observations and reports missing or unusable data explicitly.
candidate.answer: Across 250 usable trips, visitors caught an average of 1.107 fish per hour (SD 4.434). Catch rates were higher for groups using live bait (1.220 vs 0.390 fish/hour) and campers (1.347 vs 0.765 fish/hour). In the OLS model, live bait and camping were positively associated with catch rate, persons had a positive coefficient, while children and hours had negative coefficients; these are associations, not causal effects.
